items.question: Using Table 3-1 of the Utilities Accommodation Manual, what minimum cover is required for a transverse HDD installation under pavement when the drilled or reamed hole diameter is between 6 and 15 inches?
items.note: Table 3-1, HDD (transverse) sub-table, row '>6-15' inches; the row label is a sub-row under the HDD method row.

items.question: Per footnote b of Table 3-1 in the UAM, what is the minimum cover depth for a transverse HDD installation of any size under a fully controlled access roadway?
items.note: Footnote b overrides the 5 ft / 12x / 15 ft rows for fully controlled access roadways: 15 feet regardless of hole size.

items.question: If a phone company just plows its cable in along the shoulder, how many inches of cover does the UAM's open-cut bury depth table require?
items.note: Table 3-2 row 'Plowed-in communication lines/cable' = 1.5 feet; the asker's unit (inches) differs from the table's (feet).

items.question: In Table 3-3 of the UAM, what wall thickness is required for a 30-inch outside-diameter steel encasement pipe?
Table 3-3 of the UAM says a 48-inch encasement pipe needs a 0.250-inch wall. Is that right, and what is the actual required wall thickness?
items.note: False premise: 0.250 is the 14-24 inch row. Correct answer corrects the premise with 0.500 for 48 inch.

items.question: Per Table 3-4 (Steel Plate Thickness Table) in the UAM, what minimum total plate thickness is required for a trench width of 3 feet 5 inches?
My crew wants to plate over a 6-foot-wide trench overnight in the clear zone. What does the UAM say about who designs that plate?

expected.value: sealed by a North Carolina licensed Professional Engineer
accept: sealed by a licensed Professional Engineer

items.note: Spans wider than 5'-3" fall outside Table 3-4, so the plate design must be sealed by a NC licensed PE (Section 3.6.10.4).

items.question: In Table 4-1 (Utility Agreement Chart) of the UAM, which agreement covers construction when NCDOT constructs the relocation under Utilities Construction and NCDOT has cost responsibility?
items.note: Row 'NCDOT Constructs (Utilities Construction, UC)', column 'NCDOT' under the merged 'Cost Responsibility' header.

items.question: According to footnote a of Table 4-1 in the UAM, what was the Utility Engineering by Owner Agreement formerly called?
items.note: Footnote a of Table 4-1.

items.question: In the UAM's Table 4-3 estimate summary example, what salvage amount is deducted from the total billing?
items.note: Table 4-3 row 'Less salvage (if applicable)'; other rows are $360,000 (betterment credit) and $698,000 (reimbursement).

items.question: What is the minimum performance and indemnity bond amount for a utility crossing of a controlled access highway in the UAM Appendix D bond table (updated 2019)?
items.note: 'Minimum Amounts for Performance and Indemnity Bonds', utility encroachments: unpaved $5,000; paved two lane $10,000; non-C/A >2 lanes $15,000; controlled access $20,000. Page has no printed number.

items.question: In the UAM Appendix D bond minimums table, what is the minimum bond per linear foot for curb and gutter under non-utility encroachments?
items.note: Non-utility encroachments section: paving $12/sq ft, curb and gutter $18/linear ft, sidewalk $45/sq yd.

items.question: In the Blue Diamond conduit sizes table in Appendix F of the UAM, what is the nominal inside diameter of 2-inch SCH 80 conduit?
items.note: Vendor spec sheet (ASTM F 2160 SDR pipe data / SCH 40-SCH 80 block). 2" row: OD 2.375; SCH 40 ID 2.047; SCH 80 ID 1.913, wall 0.218.

items.question: Per Figure 3-3 of the UAM (clearances for aerial installations near bridges), what is the minimum sag clearance height above a bridge deck for power and telecommunications lines?
items.note: Note 2 on Figure 3-3: minimum sag clearance height is 25 feet (telecommunications and power).

items.question: Under the horizontal clearance exception in Figure 3-3 of the UAM, to what may the minimum horizontal clearance to a bridge be reduced when the power line's sag clearance above the deck is at least 45 feet and the voltage is 350 kV or less?
items.note: Note 3 of Figure 3-3; the base rule is 8 feet + Table 'A'.

items.question: Per Figure 3-2 and Section 3.4.13 of the UAM, temporary shoring is required when a theoretical 2:1 slope from the bottom of the excavation meets the existing ground closer than what distance from the outside edge of an open travel lane?
items.note: Rule text on 3-40 (p.113), figure callout '5 ft min' on 3-41 (p.114).

items.question: How high do the wires have to be when a utility line crosses over an interstate?
items.note: Section 3.3.5 (crossing a controlled access highway: 24 feet) and 3.3.3.2 item 1 state the same value; either page is correct.

items.question: Where a guardrail is present, how far behind the face of the guardrail must a street light pole be placed under standard placement in the UAM?
items.note: Section 3.3.7.9; reducible to 3 ft 6 in with 3 ft 1.5 in post spacing.

items.question: When guardrail post spacing is reduced to 3 feet 1.5 inches, how far behind the face of the guardrail may a light pole be placed per the UAM?
items.note: Section 3.3.7.9; the reduced spacing begins 25 feet before the pole.

items.question: What's the deal with fire hydrants next to the road in NCDOT right of way, how far back do they have to go?
items.note: Section 3.4.9.1: breakaway type, minimum 6 feet from back of curb and gutter / back of ditch.

items.question: Section 3.6.13 of the UAM refers to Section 2.7.6 for bond information. Under that section, how soon after satisfactory completion of the work may a performance bond be released at the earliest?
items.note: Section 2.7.6.5 Release of Bonds (p.69); the pointer is on p.137.

items.question: For a transverse utility crossing inside a reinforced concrete box culvert, above what flood water surface elevation must the crossing occur per the UAM?
items.note: Section 3.5.1.2 item 3.b.v (box culverts) = 25-year; item 3.c.i for drainage pipe says 10-year, a decoy on the same page.

items.question: We want to mole an 8-inch conduit under a driveway with a pneumatic piercing tool. What is the largest diameter the UAM allows for the driving method?
items.note: Section 3.6.8.6 Driving: diameter shall be a maximum of 6 inches, so 8 inches is not allowed.

items.question: When grouting the voids outside steel tunnel liner plates, the 2-inch grout openings in the top of the liner plates are provided on what centers?
items.note: Section 3.6.8.8.

items.question: Do we have to tell anybody at NCDOT before digging near a traffic light, and how close counts?
items.note: Section 3.6.10.2: excavations within 1,000 feet of a signalized intersection require notification to the Division Traffic Engineer. The TOC lists '3.6.10 Excavation Guidance'.

items.question: When a utility abandons a pipe in place in NCDOT right of way, how full does it have to be grouted?
items.note: Section 3.6.15.4: at least 90 percent full, or completely full on railroad right of way.

items.question: If a town of about 30,000 people has to move its water line for an NCDOT widening, what share of the non-betterment relocation cost does NCDOT pick up?
Per footnote 2 in Section 4.4.1.4 of the UAM, from what date are the provisions for private water or sewer utilities serving 10,000 or fewer customers retroactive?
items.note: Footnote 2 also defines customers as households served when the agreement is executed.

items.question: Under the UAM, for a utility to have a compensable interest by adverse possession, how long before the facilities were taken into NCDOT right of way must possession have begun?
items.note: Section 4.4.3.1. The glossary (A-1) repeats 20 years; the Aug 2026 Cost Reimbursement Guidance gives 7 years under color of title.

items.question: According to NCDOT's August 2026 Utility Cost Reimbursement Guidance, what prescriptive period applies to adverse possession under color of title?
items.note: Table row 'Adverse Possession', Definition column: 7 years under color of title or 20 years without. Conflicts with the UAM's flat 20 years. No printed page numbers in this memo.

items.question: Per the table in the 2026 Utility Cost Reimbursement Guidance, within how many years must an inverse condemnation action be brought under G.S. 40A-51(a)?
items.note: Row 'Inverse Condemnation' starts on p.3 and its Definition cell continues on p.4 where the 2-year limit appears.

items.question: For direct bury utility poles 60 feet and taller, what must the pole owner submit with the encroachment per the May 26, 2026 NCDOT memo?
items.note: Attestation that NESC Rules 250C, 250D and 250B were considered and achieved; submitted by the pole owner, not the applicant.

items.question: According to the NCDOT Standard Utility Encroachment Plan Requirements (July 2023), what is the largest scale allowed for scaled plans?
items.note: Same rule appears in UAM 3.2.1.6 (p.80) and Appendix C (p.202); the question names the standalone July 2023 document.

items.question: In the July 2023 Standard Utility Encroachment Plan Requirements, the profile view must show the theoretical 1:1 slope from the edge of pavement and a theoretical 2:1 slope taken at a point how far from the edge of the travel way?
items.note: The UAM's own profile list (p.82) only names the 1:1 slope; the 2023 standalone adds the 2:1 slope at 5 feet.

items.question: Per the general requirements on Form R/W 16.1 (Rev. Sept 2026), how far beyond the toe of slopes must encasements extend in fill sections?

items.note: Unless a written waiver is secured from NCDOT.

items.question: Per the HDD Required Information list (November 2019) in UAM Appendix F, within how many days after the drilling operation must as-built drawings be supplied to the District Engineer's office?
items.note: Item 15 of the HDD list; Appendix F holds two copies of the form (static p.273-274 and fillable p.275-276). Item 15 is on p.274 and p.276.

items.question: The HDD requirements list in UAM Appendix F says a traffic control plan is needed when personnel or equipment are within what distance of the edge of pavement on an undivided road?
